short.text: The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, where sunlight is scattered by gas molecules in the atmosphere. These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of light, such as blue and violet, more effectively than longer wavelengths like red and yellow. This scattered blue light is what we see when we look at the sky.
